open_task_policy: Accept independently verified alternative constructions, counterexamples, and unexpected results. Explicit additional-hypothesis results are legitimate contributions but must not be relabeled as completion of the original scope. A short proof using applicable standard theorems is fully acceptable. Honest incompleteness is distinct from an invalid proof.
required_evidence: Construct the Gamma-invariant quotient in the stated sheaf category and prove its universal property; account for local representatives and local equality of orbit records.
Give a necessary-and-sufficient criterion on an arbitrary Gamma-equivariant sheaf E over h_T for realization as h_T fiber-product_Q D, and prove both directions without presupposing D.

Construct realizations when the criterion holds and describe all realization morphisms, equivalently a fully faithful and essentially surjective comparison with the appropriate full subcategory of equivariant objects.
For every sheaf B over Q, prove that (h_T fiber-product_Q B)/Gamma is B and establish the corresponding classification and compatibility with pullback, including nonrepresentable B.
critical_errors: Identify the pointwise orbit presheaf with its sheaf quotient without proving the sheaf condition.
Assume the topological orbit space is Hausdorff or profinite, or assume the quotient sheaf is representable.
Treat all equivariant objects as descent data while ignoring multiple arrows over the same base relation.
Check stabilizer action only on ordinary points E(*) and infer the required equality of sheaf sections.
Select global lifts or one globally fixed group element from local orbit equality.
Establish base-change stability only for representable B, or claim arbitrary base change reflects descendability.
Claim unique realization maps without specifying compatibility with the chosen identification, thereby incorrectly eliminating automorphisms.
completion_policy: Completion requires the quotient, a correct testwise or internally equivalent stabilizer criterion, proof of the realization equivalence on objects and morphisms, and arbitrary-sheaf-base compatibility. Effective topos descent is a valid alternative if its relation and action hypotheses are explicitly verified. The dense Z action and the point-invisible action examples are optional checks of stronger claims, not mandatory tasks. A short nonfree-action counterexample alone is only a partial contribution.
